blocks.h2: How an Overhead Sewer System Works
blocks.body: Every drain below the street sewer's flow line, like your floor drain, a basement bathroom, or a laundry line, normally relies on gravity to reach the sewer. An overhead sewer system reroutes those drains into a sump pit instead. An [ejector pump](/hanover-park/ejector-pump) lifts that wastewater up to a line above flood level, where a check valve keeps it from flowing back down. From there, gravity carries it the rest of the way to the street sewer, the same as every drain upstairs.

blocks.intro: In the August 2007 storm, 3.25 inches of rain fell fast, and many basements took on sewer water.

items.body: Common in homes from the '70s and '80s.
The 2007 storm also knocked out power. An overhead sewer pump needs a battery backup or generator.
A clogged or broken line can cause backups too. A [sewer repair](/hanover-park/sewer-repair) may be enough.

blocks.h2: How an Overhead Sewer Goes In
blocks.body: First, we cut the basement floor to reach the existing drains and set a sealed pit with a pump. Basement fixtures are re-piped to drain into that pit. A new line runs up the wall and out above the flood level, then drops into the sewer outside. The old connection at the floor is closed off so sewer water can't push back in. We test with water before closing the floor. In a finished Hanover Park basement, we plan the route to touch as little finish work as possible.

blocks.h2: Overhead Sewer Questions From Hanover Park Homeowners

items.preview: For moderate risk, it can be.
items.answer: For occasional backups, often. For repeat backups or a finished basement, an overhead sewer gives full protection.

items.q: What happens in a power outage?
items.answer: The pump needs power, so a battery backup or generator is worth it. The 2007 storm showed why.

items.q: Does it stop water through the walls?
items.answer: No. That's groundwater. A [sump pump](/hanover-park/sump-pumps) handles it.
Usually a few days, depending on the layout.

items.q: Will an overhead sewer change how my basement works?
items.answer: Day to day, no. Fixtures drain normally. The difference is that the basement no longer connects directly to a sewer that can push back.
Yes. We handle the village permit for our work.
